frontier.hypothesis: H5''' -- the last two points are an allocator-INPUT residue (pseudo/priority structure) rather than a statement-shape residue, and the only untried lever is the allocno PRIORITY ORDER.
frontier.mechanism: allocno_compare priority is floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs / live_length. Route (3) -- regs_someone_prefers -- is the one exclusion mechanism that costs no instruction at all, and it is closed today only because both $a0-preferring allocnos (97 = a0_var, 102 = y) rank ABOVE 103. Anything that demotes 102 or 97 below 103 without changing the emitted instructions would open it, since both already carry the $a0 preference. The two knobs are reg_n_refs and live_length, both computable from the dump before building.
frontier.next_probe: Build variants that change y's or a0_var's REFERENCE COUNT without changing the emitted instructions (e.g. reading *(s32 *)(obj + 0x108) twice and letting CSE collapse it, or splitting `y - a0_var` / `y + a0_var` across an extra reference), and read the `;; N regs to allocate` order out of tmp/grind/func_8002EA24/s6/dump.sh BEFORE scoring: the variant only matters if 102 or 97 moves past 103 in that list. Note the demoted allocno must ALSO conflict with 103, which reintroduces the liveness cost -- verify both conditions in the dump, then score.
